```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The care burden falls disproportionately on women.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"As more women have entered the paid labor force, combining full-time work with the requirements of child and elder care has spread from working class and poor women to middle income women.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A just society must guarantee that those who need care receive it and that families are able to care for their dependents.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A right to care must also mean the right for paid caregivers to be professionally trained so they can provide humane, high-quality care, and be paid a living wage.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The United States underpays teacher aides, day care workers and in-home care providers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Coupled with often exploitative working conditions, underpayment of teacher aides, day care workers and in-home care providers results in high turnover, interrupted and all too often lower quality care.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The average day care worker in the U.S. leaves their place of employment within a year.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"In France, professionally trained, unionized preschool teachers make more than well-paid elementary school teachers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
